prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: After reading the openings I have moved from my own first choice (B039) to the candidate with the broadest and most substantive support across specialties. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the case on the table where the discovery, the principle and the consequence are all easy to state: ligand design (bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines) lowers the barrier to reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes and turns a harsh, substrate-limited reaction into a general one. Four members ranked it, three of them at first or second place, and the people who know synthesis best (Somfai, Zou, Aqvist) each call it overdue after 25-plus years of independent confirmation and industrial use. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the general catalytic method, so a two-person citation is clean and defensible to a broad audience, which matters to me as chair. It also fits the criterion I care about: a clear mechanistic principle that opened a genuinely new capability, namely routine construction of aryl amines in medicines, agrochemicals and materials.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that this is an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki), and the committee may see it as the same idea applied to a different bond. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, so priority is not entirely clean. Against that, I would also note that my own B039 had thin support and I should not defend it merely because I ranked it first. The competing B068 has more first-place votes, but its clinical validation is incomplete and its credit is split across the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B011 first as the clearest case of a method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, the natural complement to the 2010 prize, with Kosugi and Migita a minor priority question.
responses.response: I largely agree on the merit, but I would not call the 2010 overlap minor for the committee as a whole. I want us to be able to state in one sentence what is new relative to Heck, Negishi and Suzuki; I think the answer is that a C-N bond formed by amine coordination, deprotonation and reductive elimination needed different ligand design and mechanism, not just a different partner. On Kosugi, I would credit him in the narrative but not the citation, since the tin-amide reaction was not general or catalytic in the later sense. If you can show the precursor was closer to the general method than you suggest, I will reconsider.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs and molecular glues (B068) first as a clean design principle that makes undruggable proteins targetable, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core.
responses.response: I rate B068 highly on generative potential and put it fourth in my opening. My reservation is maturity and definition: no degrader is yet approved, and Chabes, Aqvist and you propose different laureate sets, which shows the discovery is not yet agreed. Handa's cereblon work is a molecular-glue strand with a different logic from Crews and Deshaies's bifunctional design. I would like you to say what single sentence the citation would be. If the committee can settle that, I would consider B068 as a strong alternative or a later-year candidate, but I do not see it overtaking B011 this year.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks machine-learned interatomic potentials (B001) first as a game-changer for simulation, and also ranks B011 second and B068 third, with Parrinello as the natural anchor.
responses.response: I take seriously that B001 changes what can be simulated, and Parrinello could be recognised through another route. My concern is the attribution I read in your own text: the Behler-Parrinello and Csanyi lineages are separate, and foundation-scale potentials are still being tested for transferability. That is both an attribution and a maturity question, and only you and Zou ranked it. I am glad that B011 is your second choice, since that gives it support from synthesis and computation both. Does a combined configuration with B011 interest you, or would you keep B001 alone?

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular phase separation (B019) first as a physical-chemical organising principle, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
responses.response: As a physicist I find the polymer-physics framing attractive, and I did place B019 sixth. But I am more cautious than you on timing, since the debate on which condensates are liquid and functionally relevant is open, and we have a risk of citing a principle whose physiological scope is unsettled. I also share your worry that the natural home may be physiology. Convince me on which specific observations are now beyond dispute.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives to the 2010 cross-coupling prize when judging novelty of C-N coupling.
Whether Kosugi's precursor deserves any place in the citation.
Whether B068 should be split into PROTAC and molecular-glue strands or treated as one discovery, and whether it will have matured by next year.
Whether a two-part configuration pairing B011 with another achievement can respect the three-person limit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Lund physicist and colleague of Somfai and Sparr, but have no stated personal or institutional link to the Buchwald, Hartwig, PROTAC or sequencing candidates.
